objects.b: nenbakraniya.pdf — Nen Bakraniya, Accurate Proteome-wide Missense Variant Effect Prediction with AlphaMissense (student study deck, 37 pp)

hypotheses.name: genre-pair
hypotheses.statement: Both documents belong to the AI-model-report genre (model description, data, evaluation, limitations) while occupying disjoint domains (language vs proteome).
hypotheses.check: vocabulary overlap 0.6984 inflated by the deck's tiny 305-word vocabulary; genre words survive (model 505/11, predict 46/14, limitation 21/5); domain words are mutually exclusive (language 177/0, safety 93/0 vs missense 0/25, pathogen 1/7). No citation either way.

hypotheses.name: generation-versus-verification
hypotheses.statement: The pair instantiates the two poles of AI: GPT-4 predicts the next token (generation); AlphaMissense checks which missense variants are pathogenic (verification).
hypotheses.check: a: next-token prediction, benchmark/evaluation-heavy (evaluat* 105, benchmark 38); b: variant effect prediction (variant 21, missense 25, pathogen 7).

hypotheses.name: primary-versus-derived
hypotheses.statement: One document is the primary source (the lab's own 100-page report); the other is a derived study deck whose meaning is largely visual.
hypotheses.check: pages 100 vs 37; words 46,637 vs 624 (17 words/page); the deck's text layer is sparse — its figures carry most of its content.

hypotheses.name: predictability-bridge
hypotheses.statement: Both systems are prediction machines; the shared virtue is making outcomes checkable (predictable scaling vs proteome-wide variant effect prediction).
hypotheses.check: a: performance predicted from 1/1000th compute (predictable scaling); b: variant effects predicted proteome-wide. Prediction appears 46/14 across the pair.
